observations: CSharp Linux stdout treats short writes as failure; stderr loops on positive partial progress and fails on zero or negative progress.
CSharp process ok_state preserves earlier failure through subsequent successful writes and final stdout flush.
SLG Linux stdout is unbuffered, with no pending bytes in flush_stdout. Both ordinary and parallel direct writes currently ignore write result.
SLG Linux stderr ignores write result; main unconditionally returns zero.

Ordinary imported runtime.readInt resolves to Linux RuntimeFunctionSymbols wrapper in llvm/runtime.slg, not the Wasm-only builtin read_int helper. This wrapper prints prompt then calls getchar without checking prompt output.
decision: Keep existing SLG unbuffered Linux architecture; buffered-prefix branch checks are CSharp-only and are not SLG runtime checks.
Use sticky failure state for Linux text IO; only failures store true, with atomic accesses because parallel output may fail concurrently.
Check complete stdout single writes, retry positive stderr partial writes; preserve continuation and final exit1 rather than trap.
Provide checked printing for the Linux readInt prompt; skip getchar and return zero on prompt failure. Earlier unrelated stderr failure must not suppress a later healthy prompt/read.
Keep Windows/Wasm text emitters and Linux parsing algorithm unchanged.
nextGate: Implement then format, canonical semantic preflight, source-emitter paired focused runtime; full-native consumer remains pending
